title: Sequence-length aware kernel tuner for heterogeneous GPU fleets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an autotuning service that picks the optimal kernel + quantization profile per request class by combining offline microbenchmarks with an online lightweight bandit. The tuner must account for model architecture, sequence length distribution (prefill vs decode), per-GPU memory bandwidth and SM/memory asymmetry, and fallbacks for heavy tail requests. Deliver a runtime-side decision API and a workflow for offline profiling and gated rollout.
background: Current kernel selection is static and derived from microbenchmarks at a fixed sequence length. This causes suboptimal choices for workloads where prefill (long seqlen) and decode (short, many single-token steps) behaviors differ. We also observe heterogeneity across our Dedicated fleet (A100 40GB, A100 80GB, H100, and partner T4 nodes). Early experiments indicate up to 30% variance in per-token cost when mismatched kernels/profiles are used. This ticket extends earlier kernel-routing work to make decisions seqlen- and architecture-aware, with an online tuner to adapt to workload shifts.
goals: Design a compact feature vector for requests (model, seqlen-prefill, seqlen-decode-pattern, quant-mode candidates, gpu-family)
Implement offline profiler that outputs kernel/quant performance table across seqlen and batch sizes
Integrate online tuner (epsilon-greedy bandit with decay) in the serving runtime for per-customer policy
Expose decision telemetry to Console and add a rollout plan with canary metrics
Provide migration/fallback rules to avoid regressions under tail latency spikes
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner service returns kernel+quant recommendation within 2ms per decision in the hot path
End-to-end percentiles: P50 token latency improves or unchanged; P95 latency not worse than baseline by >5% during canary
Cost-per-token reduction of >=8% on avg for mixed seqlen workloads in Dedicated A/B test
Dashboard shows per-model, per-seqlen decisions and offers rollback to previous policy
Design doc + infra tests + at least one merged runtime PR and one merged profiler PR
decisions: Use lightweight epsilon-greedy bandit for online adaptation instead of full contextual bandit to limit runtime overhead
Keep offline profiler as source-of-truth and seed online priors with stratified seqlen buckets (<=64, 65-512, 513-2048, >2048)
Quantization profiles will be treated as orthogonal axes in the candidate set; tuner may recommend 'int8-fast' vs 'int8-balanced' vs 'fp16' depending on GPU family
Fallback policy: when P95 latency exceeds SLA window, revert to baseline kernel selection for that model until degradation clears
tradeoffs: Online bandit is less sample-efficient than a contextual model but cheaper to run and easier to reason about for rollouts
Fine-grained per-tenant policies increase memory/config surface but enable better economics for high-variance customers
Profiling many (kernel,quant,seqlen,batch) combinations is expensive; we will sparsely sample and interpolate using simple regression models
tasks: T1: Define request feature schema and decision API (runtime contract)
T2: Implement and bootstrap offline profiler across GPU families (A100-40, A100-80, H100, T4)
T3: Build lightweight on-node tuner library and integrate decision call into dispatcher
T4: Add telemetry events for selected candidate, offline-prior used, sample reward (latency/cost), and fallback triggers
T5: Run Dedicated canary against 10% of traffic for three models (llama-13b, mixtral-8x7b, redwood-mini) and capture cost/latency impact
T6: Write playbook for emergency rollback and runbook for interpreting tuner drift alerts
